name: hcapp_findRunForTrack
description: Which run does an imported GPX file belong to (E5.F5.S6)? Given a track's first and last point times (UTC) and its first point's position, returns the runs that started between three hours before the first point and the last point, nearest start first, with the distance from each run's recorded start to that first point, whether the caller already has a PackTrack trail on it, and their attendance state. The app applies the rule: a run with a recorded location must be within a mile; one with no location is accepted on time alone after the user confirms. Server-side because the phone only holds runs for followed kennels and the last ten days. 1.0.1: delegates to nonApi_findRunForTrack so the server-side import processor matches identically.

parameters.name: firstPointUtc
parameters.description: Capture time of the track's first point, UTC. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

parameters.name: lastPointUtc
parameters.description: Capture time of the track's last point, UTC. Must not precede firstPointUtc. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: First point's latitude. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: First point's longitude. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: On auth failure (ValidateAppAuth, spNumber 95) or an invalid span/position (errorCode 1295, errorType 12, logged at line 72): { success = 0, errorCode, errorType }, followed by the error detail at index 1. Mutually exclusive with CandidateRuns.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: 1295 = firstPointUtc/lastPointUtc/latitude/longitude missing or out of range (lastPointUtc before firstPointUtc, |lat| > 90, |lon| > 180); 1195 / 1295 / 1395 from ValidateAppAuth.

rowsets.description: After the ErrorEnvelope on any failure.

rowsets.name: CandidateRuns
rowsets.description: On success, rowset 0 and the only rowset (no success envelope — the client tells the two shapes apart by column name). Produced by HC6.nonApi_findRunForTrack: up to 10 live, visible runs (deleted = 0, removed = 0, IsVisible = 1) whose EventStartDateTimeGmt lies in [firstPointUtc - 3h, lastPointUtc], nearest start to the first point first. Empty when nothing started in the window.

columns.name: eventId
columns.description: HC.Event.id — the Table Storage partition key, lowercased by the app.

columns.name: eventStartLocal
columns.description: Local wall-clock start (spurious offset stripped) for display.

columns.name: hasLocation
columns.description: 1 when the event has a recorded, non-zero Latitude/Longitude.

columns.name: distanceMeters
columns.description: Metres from the event's recorded start to the track's first point; NULL when hasLocation = 0.

columns.name: existingTrackPoints
columns.description: The caller's HasherEventMap.TrackPointCount on this run (0 when none) — a track already exists when > 0.

columns.name: attendenceState
columns.description: The caller's attendance state on this run (0 when no row).

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.nonApi_findRunForTrack — the matching rule shared with the server-side import processor (ProcessTrackImport); its own CATCH logs and re-throws.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on an invalid span/position (1295, line 72) and, with THROW, on an unhandled error (line 92).

codeSmells.detail: These parameters have no SQL default, so a call that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs (unlogged empty 500): @deviceId, @accessToken. On 2026-10-13 every parameter whose body already handled NULL (and every sync watermark) was given a default; these remain because they are the auth pair or the body never checks them for NULL.

codeSmells.issue: Success and error replies have different shapes
codeSmells.detail: Success returns CandidateRuns alone at index 0 (no envelope); failure returns { success = 0, ... } then the error detail. The app must sniff the first column to know which it got.
Line 32 sets NOCOUNT only. Harmless for a read, inconsistent with the HC6 standard.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
